Chakasaponin Ii is shown to have a target relationship with Solute carrier organic anion transporter family member 1B3, through two distinct pathways. In the first pathway, Chakasaponin Ii acts on 11-cis retinol dehydrogenase, which in turn targets Solute carrier organic anion transporter family member 1B3. This suggests a potential role for Chakasaponin Ii in modulating the activity of the transporter, possibly by influencing the metabolic pathways of retinoids. In the second pathway, Chakasaponin Ii directly targets CMP-N-acetylneuraminate-beta-1,4-galactoside alpha-2,3-sialyltransferase, which also leads to Solute carrier organic anion transporter family member 1B3. This indicates that Chakasaponin Ii may exert its effects through multiple molecular mechanisms, potentially affecting the transport of anionic compounds across cellular membranes.

The evidence suggests that Chakasaponin Ii may influence the function of Solute carrier organic anion transporter family member 1B3 by targeting enzymes involved in the synthesis or modification of substrates that are transported by this transporter. The two distinct pathways highlight the complexity of the relationship, with Chakasaponin Ii acting as a modulator of different enzymatic processes that ultimately affect the transporter. The integration of these pathways supports the hypothesis that Chakasaponin Ii could have a role in regulating the transport of anionic compounds, potentially with implications for drug metabolism or transport-related diseases. The presence of multiple targets and pathways underscores the need for further mechanistic investigation to fully understand the biological relevance of this relationship.
